# requireFunctionLike

<link-summary>Returns the value as a callable value, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireFunctionLike() — Returns the value as a callable value, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireFunctionLike( value: unknown, message: string = "Expected a function." // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-function-type ): Function;
```

The cheap test — `typeof value === "function"` — which is what you want before calling something. `isFunction` is the stricter reading of the same question.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                         | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------ | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                           | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a function."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`Function` — the same value, typed as a callable value.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                  |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not callable. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireFunctionLike(function () {}); // => function () {}
requireFunctionLike(Math.max); // => Math.max
requireFunctionLike(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireFunctionLike({}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
